title: Peter the Great Interrogating the Tsarevich Alexei Petrovich at Peterhof

slides.headline: A father. A son. One deadly question.
slides.sub: Nikolai Ge, Peter the Great Interrogating the Tsarevich Alexei, 1871

slides.headline: Peterhof, 1718
slides.text: Peterhof, 1718. In his seaside palace, Monplaisir, Peter the Great confronts his son and heir, Tsarevich Alexei. This is no family chat.

slides.headline: The son who ran
slides.text: In 1716, Alexei had fled abroad, to the Emperor in Vienna, then to Naples. To his father, it was betrayal of the worst kind.

slides.headline: The promise
slides.text: So Peter sent an envoy with a promise: come home, and you won't be punished. Alexei believed it and came back. Big mistake.

slides.headline: Papers on the table
slides.text: Now look at the table. Papers spill across it, one onto the floor. One historian read them as testimony from Afrosinya, the woman Alexei loved.

slides.headline: Eyes lowered
slides.text: Meanwhile, Alexei can't meet his father's gaze. Pale, silent, eyes down, he waits. Peter just stares, the evidence at his elbow.

slides.headline: The final game
slides.text: Look down: some see this black-and-white floor as a chessboard, Alexei's final game. The red and black tablecloth? Colours of mourning.

slides.headline: The verdict
slides.text: And then the verdict. In June 1718, 127 senators and officials sentenced Alexei to death. His own father had brought him home.

slides.headline: Father and son
slides.text: Two days later, Alexei died in the Peter and Paul Fortress, after interrogation and torture. Was Peter a just ruler, or a cruel father?
